track_source: static symbol comparison of built images; no board involved
asked_by: owner: why are old firmwares with malloc being tested at all
findings: the tip links no allocator at all: malloc and _sbrk are absent from 4dc944a, present in all four older images. 4455426 removed the last reference and with it the allocator, so test_no_heap is now a structural guarantee rather than a behavioural one
the older images link it because printf/snprintf pull it in - it is not evidence that anything allocated on the working path, which is what invariant 7 forbids

the allocator is NOT a confound in the per-image phase: all four images that link it read four different phases (135, 156, 177, 5), and the tip without it reads 156 - the same phase as 8e300d2 with it
bss end is identical at 20084000 across all five, so the heap start does not move
why_old_images_were_flashed: bisect arms for #5 only. Establishing that the displacement is a function of the image, and attributing the bound crossing to 398ac94, requires flashing the historical images - a bisect necessarily executes old code. No claim about what should ship.
verdict: seventh mechanism eliminated: allocator presence does not select the phase
